counterfactual_missing_items: Normal EMG at rest with no electrical myotonia
No significant family history of neuromuscular disorders
decisive_items: High-arched palate, elongated face with dolichocephaly
Giant motor unit potential and neuropathic changes in proximal and distal muscles
progressive muscle weakness starting in lower limbs then upper limbs
response.rationale: R4 captures the most specific phenotypic features (facial dysmorphism, neuropathic EMG changes) and the progressive weakness pattern, but is weakened by the absence of myotonia and normal reflexes. R2 has less specific support (low birth weight, delayed milestones) and is contradicted by normal acid alpha-glucosidase. R1 is too non-specific and contradicted by normal reflexes and sensory exam.

rejected.why: Only one support span (progressive weakness) and contradicted by normal reflexes and sensory exam; lacks specificity.
